note: v3: same claim, same candidate set, same thresholds as v2. Amended AFTER v2 results were seen; the candidate was chosen by simulation, with its criteria and file hashes recorded before it was run on real data (protocols/v3_decision/DECISION_before_real.md).

policies.rule: k limited to the draws every question has; k >= 2 only with answer keys; cut values = fractions 0.25/0.5 of the SMALL model's generation cap AND absolute token budgets (powers of two 512..32768) strictly below that cap
policies.abstain_note: ABSTAIN is excluded from the primary claim: without a coverage requirement a policy could 'save' by not answering. A coverage-constrained claim is future work.

cost.lambda_rule_for_tokens: lambda = parameter count of big / parameter count of small (compute per token); report also break-even lambda (R4)
cost.c_max_rule: tokens: generation caps from meta.json; usd/gpu_s: the cap in tokens times the largest per-token price of the pair (stated in the config)

measure_rules.usd: c_max = (cap_small + max prompt tokens) x max price per token of small + the same for big (price per token = cost_usd/(in+out), from cost and token columns); skipped when either model is in locally_run_models (LLMRouterBench ran its 7-9B models on its own GPUs; their cost field is an estimate whose method the source does not state)
measure_rules.tokens_lambda1: raw token counts, lambda = 1 (a reference: saves only if the small model writes fewer tokens)
measure_rules.tokens_params: lambda = parameters used per generated token, big / small: total for dense models, ACTIVATED for mixture-of-experts (compute per token)

pairs.rule: every pair (small, big) of the same source and benchmark where big has more parameters (or a higher price if parameters are unknown) and both models answered >= n_min common questions; NOT chosen by outcome
pairs.report: number of pairs AND number of distinct models and benchmarks (pairs share models; not independent experiments)
pairs.primary_rule: same family / vendor, smaller or cheaper -> larger or dearer; listed from model NAMES before any audit
pairs.secondary_rule: every ordered pair of the pool where the big model has a larger nominal parameter count (nominal_params_b, when both are listed) or else a higher median billed price per token (cost_usd/(in+out)); equal or unknown -> no pair

params_sources.dense 8-9B: Hugging Face model pages (parameter count of the safetensors): Qwen3-8B 8.19B, DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B 8.19B, Intern-S1-mini 8.54B, GLM-Z1-9B-0414 9.40B
params_sources.qwen3-235b-a22b: 22B activated (model name A22B; 235.1B total on Hugging Face)
params_sources.deepseek-r1-0528: 37B activated of 671B (DeepSeek-V3 architecture; 684.5B on Hugging Face incl. MTP) - VERIFY in the paper
params_sources.glm-4.6: 32B activated, ~355-357B total (third-party listing; VERIFY against the official model card)

pairs.primary_exclude_reason: multi-step agent tasks: one 'question' is a whole episode with tool calls; small-first-then-escalate on a finished episode is not the single-turn question answering the claim is about

criteria.a: fraction of configurations with verdict GO
criteria.b: number of configurations where the point-estimate rule (cheapest policy with empirical risk <= alpha and empirical saving >= s on all data) says GO but the audit does not
criteria.c: number of configurations whose verdict changes between cost measures (R3)
criteria.d: evidence gap (R4) in the INCONCLUSIVE configurations: questions needed for BOTH legs at power 0.8 (median and range), and the number unreachable with these candidates
criteria.if_not_notable: report as is; most-INCONCLUSIVE is itself a finding; no threshold changes after seeing results; findings after looking are labelled exploratory with the number of comparisons tried
criteria.b_naive_rule: naive GO iff some candidate policy has empirical risk <= alpha and empirical saving >= s on ALL data (no split, no interval, no correction)

test_split: our Qwen test split is opened once, after the tag protocol-freeze (15/12/2026)

benchmarks.rule: every (source, benchmark) pool; a pair enters only with >= pairs.n_min common questions
benchmarks.exclude_reason: correctness from an LLM judge (source: LLMRouterBench Table 9): the judge's own error is not covered; reported as tier 'excluded'
benchmarks.excluded_run: not audited in the main run (crossmap --tier both); --tier excluded gives an exploratory run

data_rules.finish_length: a generation with finish = length has no answer (escalated by the replay)
data_rules.finish_other: finish missing -> 'unknown'; content_filter / engine_overloaded are kept as answers graded by the source (conservative for GO)
data_rules.lrb_caps: LLMRouterBench states no max_tokens: cap = smallest power of two >= the largest completion_tokens of the model on the benchmark (token counts only)
data_rules.lrb_question_identity: a question whose text hash differs between models is dropped
data_rules.monkey: first 64 of 10,000 samples per problem; token counts MEASURED with the model family's own tokenizer when it is supplied (Llama-3 for Llama-3-*, Gemma for Gemma-*, GPT-NeoX for Pythia-*; special tokens not added; tokenizer file sha256 recorded per model in meta.token_source), else ESTIMATED = ceil(chars/4); output clipped at the source's cap; answer keys = extracted final answers, canonicalized when votes are counted
data_rules.lurume: k = 1; cost_usd = official_usd (billed); cap = the largest of requested_max_tokens and the observed output of the model on the benchmark (the source reports outputs above the requested maximum: deepseek-v4-flash up to 515,083 > 384,000 in 100 rows); rows kept, count in meta.notes
data_rules.price_rows: the largest price per token of a model counts rows with zero output tokens (a billed prompt) too
data_rules.answer_equivalence_exact: exact = whitespace collapsed, case folded, $...$ / \\boxed{...} / a final period removed, plain decimal numbers written canonically (18 = 18.0; 1,000 = 1000); applied when votes are counted

run.command: python -m caac.pool_v1.crossmap POOLS --lock protocols/audit_lock_v3.json --out map_v3/   (default --tier both)
run.primary_claims: tier primary only; secondary and excluded are reported as supporting / exploratory

sensitivity.rule: every primary configuration is also audited at each (alpha, s) cell; all cells are reported, whatever their verdict; the main result is the cell (audit.alpha, audit.s) and is never replaced by another cell

reporting.primary: one row per configuration (pool x pair x cost measure): verdict, chosen policy, naive verdict, questions needed; plus the sensitivity grid
reporting.secondary: aggregate only: verdict shares per source and overall, criteria a-d; descriptive (pairs share models and questions); never quoted as a single-pair claim
reporting.excluded: LLM-judged benchmarks: listed with configuration counts; not audited in the main run (optional exploratory run, labelled as such)
reporting.multiplicity: each verdict carries its own guarantee at level delta; no family-wise correction across configurations; the number of configurations is always reported next to any count of GO
reporting.dry_run_25_11: structure-only listing before freezing: 13,126 configurations = 80 primary (10 pairs, 40 pair-pool cells, 2 measures each), 9,666 secondary, 3,380 excluded; lurume_aime dropped (22 questions < n_min)
reporting.v1_and_v2: v1 = the run registered first (reported in full, as is); v2 = amended after v1 was seen, reported beside it with the amendment list; claims of the paper rest on v2 for public sources and on the single opening of our test split
reporting.v1_v2_v3: v1 = registered first, v2 = amended after v1, v3 = amended after v2 (see amendments v3-1..v3-4); all three reported side by side; claims of the paper rest on v3 for public sources and on the single opening of our test split

supersedes: audit_lock_v2.json (tag audit-lock-v2-final, commit 35f3706, hash 5a542f87...) for the verdict procedure; v1 and v2 results stay reported beside v3

amendments.what: cut grid: absolute token budgets 512..32768 added to the cap fractions
amendments.why: with caps of 128k-384k tokens, cuts at 25%/50% of the cap never act, so on k = 1 sources every candidate was 'always the small model'

amendments.what: LLMRouterBench: usd skipped for locally run 7-9B models; tokens_params (activated parameters) added
amendments.why: the source does not state how it priced its locally run models (noted in MASTER 12.32 before v1 was frozen)

amendments.what: Lurume cap covers the observed output; largest price per token counts zero-output rows
amendments.why: the cost bound c_max must hold for every row; the secondary v1 run stopped on a row above it (data defect, found after v1)

amendments.what: R4 gives a planning estimate (or 'unreachable with these candidates') when no policy passed half A
amendments.why: criterion d was empty in v1; reporting only, verdicts unaffected

amendments.what: answer keys compared after canonical number / wrapper normalization
amendments.why: exact string comparison split equivalent answers into different votes (changes 9.4% of Monkey MATH keys, 0.85% of GSM8K)

amendments.what: swe_bench_verified and tau2_test: declared pairs become secondary
amendments.why: multi-step agent episodes, not single-turn questions; decided from task structure

amendments.what: Monkey token counts measured with each model family's tokenizer (estimate kept only where a tokenizer is not supplied)
amendments.why: the source has no token counts; a measured count removes the estimate from the cost measure

amendments.what: no A/B split: every policy tested on ALL questions, each leg at delta/|Pi| (Bonferroni = Learn-then-Test form); GO if any passes, report the cheapest passing policy
amendments.why: v2 selected on half A and tested on half B, wasting half the data and choosing near-boundary policies that then failed B; simulated GO power 0.21->0.99 (pi24_feasible, n=600), all wrong-verdict rates <= 0.035

amendments.what: structural range of the cost difference d: an escalated question costs its small part plus exactly its big-only cost, so d in [-(a_max + max(s,0) b_max), (1-s) b_max] instead of [-c_max, (1-s) c_max]
amendments.why: the v2 range was looser than the data allow; the betting test's power depends on the range; verified on every real configuration by assertion

amendments.what: R4 replaced by the evidence gap: questions needed for BOTH legs at power 0.8, same tests, tested at delta/|Pi|, planned on the best-looking candidate; 'unreachable' otherwise
amendments.why: v2 R4 covered the risk leg only and at ~50% power; following it led to a GO in 4-28% of simulated pilots versus 75-84% with the evidence gap

amendments.what: certified frontier reported as supplementary: per policy one-sided Clopper-Pearson risk bound and betting saving bound over a fixed s grid, each at delta/(2|Pi|)
amendments.why: gives the largest certified saving at each alpha; does not enter the verdict

freeze_rule: status becomes 'frozen' and frozen_on is set in the commit tagged audit-lock-v3, before our Qwen test split is opened
